findings.issue_text: [BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), but _truncate_title is defined as a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration, not on PRCommentWorkflow, so every invocation raises AttributeError: type object 'PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title'. Any caller of this helper (GitHub/GitLab merged-PR comment generation) crashes with AttributeError before the comment body can be built; the PR comment is never posted.

[BUG] GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body invokes self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue), but both methods were added to CommitContextIntegration and GitHubPRCommentWorkflow subclasses PRCommentWorkflow (a separate helper class that composes the integration), so neither method exists on self. The first merged-PR comment generated after this change raises AttributeError ('GitHubPRCommentWorkflow' object has no attribute 'get_merged_pr_single_issue_template'), so PR comment posting fails at runtime instead of rendering the new environment-aware template.

[BUG] GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body invokes self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue), which are defined on CommitContextIntegration, not on GitlabPRCommentWorkflow's actual base class PRCommentWorkflow. GitLab merged-PR comment generation raises AttributeError at runtime; the comment is never posted.

[ADVISORY] The migration bodies of 0917 and 0920 are replaced with no-ops that defer to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py, but that file is not added anywhere in this diff's visible changes. If 0921 is not present in the repository (not added in this PR and not already merged), the org-saved-searches-to-views data conversion silently never executes on any deployment, leaving users without their converted views; verify the file exists and is ordered after 0920.

[ADVISORY] Same no-op stub as 0917: the commented dependency 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py is not visible in this diff, and the stubs' claim that the migrations were 'never run' is unverifiable for deployments that already executed the previously-merged 0917/0920. If 0921 does not exist, conversion never happens; additionally, deployments that did run the old 0917 already produced GroupSearchView rows with the old (owner-less) logic, and the stub comments give no mechanism to reconcile that data with 0921's output.

[ADVISORY] The four new x-programs commands (eap-spans-subscription-results, subscription-results-eap-items, metrics-subscription-results, generic-metrics-subscription-results) assume `sentry run consumer <name>` accepts these names, which requires each name to be registered in sentry's consumer registry (sentry.consumers). If any of these consumer names is not registered (e.g. the EAP/metrics subscription-results consumers land in a different PR or under a different name), `devservices up` for the tracing dependency set launches programs that crash immediately with an unrecognized-consumer error, breaking local dev startup for everyone using the tracing mode.

[ADVISORY] The new snuba-metrics devservice references remote mode 'containerized-metrics-dev' in the getsentry/snuba repo, a mode name whose existence in snuba's devservices configuration is assumed but not established (the only pre-existing mode referenced for this repo is 'containerized-profiles'). If snuba's devservices config does not define a 'containerized-metrics-dev' mode, `devservices up` for the tracing dependency set fails to resolve the snuba-metrics service, so the new tracing profile cannot start at all.

[BUG] The PR is titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System' but contains no bulk-delete implementation at all — the only replay-delete change is a null-guard for max_segment_id (rows with max_segment_id None now return [] instead of crashing on range(max_segment_id+1)); no bulk endpoint, no self-serve UI, no batch orchestration exists anywhere in the diff. Reviewers and operators cannot validate the stated feature against this diff: the promised system is either entirely missing (under-scoped PR) or hidden among ~20 unrelated change areas, so the actual bulk-delete behavior ships unreviewed in some other change while this PR claims to be it.

[ADVISORY] Migrations 0917 and 0920 are gutted to no-ops whose replacement, '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py', does not exist anywhere in this diff. If this PR merges before (or without) the PR containing 0921, every deployment that runs 0917/0920 after this commit permanently skips the org-saved-search-to-view conversion with no backfill path in the shipped history; the data migration is also completely untraceable to the replay bulk-delete intent.

[ADVISORY] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT is flipped from 'low' to 'off' (and the matching projectoptions default at src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205) with no traceable requirement in a replay bulk-delete PR. This silently disables automatic Seer autofix for every new project on deploy — a product-behavior change riding unflagged inside an unrelated PR, so it will not be caught by anyone reviewing the stated feature and cannot be reverted without knowing it is here.

[ADVISORY] A brand-new preprod analytics event (PreprodArtifactApiAssembleEvent) plus instrumentation in organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py is introduced here with no connection to replays bulk delete. New observability surface for the preprod feature ships without its own review context; if the preprod feature's analytics requirements change, this PR's changelog/review history will not reflect why this event exists.

[ADVISORY] The entire browser-reporting collector is rewritten from a dataclass to a DRF serializer with per-report validation and new 422 error bodies — unrelated to replays bulk delete. A behavioral change to a public ingestion endpoint (per-report rejection with detailed error payloads instead of blanket 422) hides inside an unrelated PR; regressions in browser report ingestion will be attributed to a PR whose title says replays.

[ADVISORY] Detector validators gain a new owner (ActorField) API surface with create/update/clear semantics — no requirement in this PR's stated scope. A new public API capability (assigning detector owners via the detector endpoint) ships without its own review, tests-traceability, or changelog entry; API consumers and the workflow-engine team cannot connect this behavior change to the replay PR that introduced it.

[ADVISORY] The delayed-workflow processor is refactored (dcg_to_slow_conditions hoisted, new no_slow_condition_groups logging, event_data logging fix) — entirely unrelated work bundled into this diff. Changes to the workflow firing hot path (including a behavioral logging change keyed on DCGs whose slow conditions disappeared mid-flight) receive review only from people examining a replay PR; a regression here delays or drops workflow notifications for all users.

[ADVISORY] The replay summarize-breadcrumbs endpoint is expanded to fetch error IDs via Snuba and error details via nodestore and interleave them into the Seer prompt — a separate replay feature that is not the bulk delete system the PR title names. This adds two new network dependencies (Snuba query_replay_instance, nodestore get_multi) on the summarize path; if this feature has defects (e.g., error-timestamp interleaving or missing-event handling), they are reviewed under the wrong feature banner and the bulk-delete review never sees them.

[ADVISORY] devservices gains a snuba-metrics service and four subscription-results consumer programs wired into a new 'tracing' dependency profile — infrastructure work with no relation to replay bulk delete. Every developer's local environment now spins up additional containers by default via the tracing profile; local resource usage and dev-env breakage from these consumers will be attributed to a replay PR, making bisect and revert decisions wrong.

[ADVISORY] ParameterizationRegexExperiment is deleted, ParameterizationExperiment is narrowed to the callable variant, the isinstance branch is removed, and the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option is unregistered — a grouping-feature cleanup unrelated to replays. If any deployed grouping config still references the regex experiment form, run() now calls experiment.run(content, _incr_counter) with a regex-shaped callable contract and the removed option silently stops sampling; this behavior change is invisible to reviewers scoped to the replay feature.

[ADVISORY] The feedback-summary LLM prompt is substantially rewritten (join separator, 55-word cap, theme-priority guidance) inside a replay bulk-delete PR. User-visible AI summary output for user feedback changes with no traceable requirement; prompt-quality regressions discovered later cannot be tied to the change that introduced them.

[ADVISORY] Processing deadlines (30/300/120s) are added to webhook delivery tasks and a 60s deadline to check_auth_identities (src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py:73-77) with no stated requirement. Long webhook deliveries that previously ran to completion will now be killed at the new deadlines and retried; production webhook behavior changes under a PR whose reviewers were evaluating replay deletion.

[ADVISORY] PR-comment issue templates are restructured (merged-PR template moved to commit_context, title truncation at 50 chars, environment info appended) across GitHub/GitLab integrations — unrelated feature work in this diff. The user-visible format of PR bot comments changes (titles truncated, environment appended, bullet character changed from '-' to '*') without any requirement in scope; a formatting regression in PR comments will be hunted for in a replay PR.

[ADVISORY] A batch of frontend refactors (FlexSpacer/FlexContainer replaced by shared Flex in codeSnippet, codecov selectors, eventAttachments, chonk button transition timing, groupingVariant tooltip removal) is bundled in with no relation to the stated backend feature. Visual/UX changes (removed 'Type' tooltips in grouping info, 0.1s→0.06s button transition) ship inside a replay PR, so frontend reviewers who filter by feature area will never examine them and any layout regression is mis-attributed on bisect.

[BUG] fetch_error_details materializes every error event for a replay via an unbounded nodestore get_multi: error_ids comes straight from the Snuba response with no LIMIT/cap, and node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(...) for id in error_ids] issues one bulk fetch of all of them on a synchronous user-facing GET. A replay associated with hundreds or thousands of errors (the exact replays a user would want summarized) makes the endpoint fetch all of their nodestore documents into memory and embed all of their messages into the Seer request payload, turning a bounded paginated segment read into an unbounded fan-out that times out or OOMs the API worker on the busiest replays.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's error-context feature silently depends on the client passing field=error_ids: response[0].get("error_ids", []) reads a key that process_raw_response only emits when 'error_ids' is among request.query_params.getlist("field"). Any caller of this GET that does not include error_ids in the field query param gets an empty error_ids list and a breadcrumb summary silently missing all error context — the feature degrades to the old behavior with no error or signal, and the frontend/integration contract now requires an undocumented query parameter to function.

[ADVISORY] The Snuba query_replay_instance call and the nodestore error fetch both run before the enable_error_context check, so a caller that disables error context still pays for the replay-instance Snuba query, and every paginated page request repeats both fetches. Callers that explicitly pass enable_error_context=false to avoid error work still incur the full Snuba query on every request, and clients paginating through segments re-run the Snuba query and nodestore fetch once per page, multiplying hot-path cost by the number of pages for data that does not change between pages.

[ADVISORY] enable_error_context is parsed with strict string equality (request.query_params.get("enable_error_context", "true").lower() == "false"), a stringly-typed boolean with no option or feature-flag gate. Clients sending 0, no, or off get error fetching enabled anyway (the value is silently ignored), and if the Seer call behind this feature degrades, it cannot be disabled without a code deploy since there is no options-register knob backing it.

[ADVISORY] fetch_error_details catches Exception and returns [], conflating 'nodestore fetch failed' with 'this replay has no errors' in the value consumed by gen_request_data. When nodestore is degraded or node_ids are malformed, users receive a breadcrumb summary that silently omits every error with no user-visible indication, while the only trace is a captured Sentry event — operators cannot distinguish data absence from a systemic fetch failure via the product surface.

[BUG] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) executes at the top of post() before the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature check and before any request validation, so the event is recorded for requests that are subsequently rejected. The analytics metric counts assemble attempts from organizations without the feature enabled and malformed/failed requests as successful assemble events, inflating adoption/funnel numbers for the preprod feature precisely for the population that has not rolled out.

[ADVISORY] The collector validates each report against a strict closed enum (ChoiceField over BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) and URLField, and rejects the entire request batch with 422 on the first invalid report. When a browser ships a new Reporting-API report type (the spec explicitly evolves report types) or a url outside URLField's http/https scheme allowlist (e.g. chrome-error:// or blob URLs on crash reports), the whole payload is dropped with a 422 — including every valid deprecation/crash report in the same batch — so ingestion silently loses data for spec evolution and the endpoint needs a code change per new report type instead of tolerating unknown types.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation tuning default "off" is now duplicated in two independently maintained sources of truth: DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in constants.py and register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default="off") in projectoptions/defaults.py, both edited in this diff and neither referencing the other. The next change to this default will be applied to one copy and not the other (the parallel-enumeration drift the previous "low" copies already invited), silently giving new projects a different automation tuning depending on which code path reads the default.

[ADVISORY] This diff removes the only call sites of format_comment_subtitle (here and in gitlab/integration.py lines 251-258) while leaving the method defined, so a public method of the PR comment workflow classes is now dead code. Out-of-tree subclasses or integrations that override/call format_comment_subtitle keep compiling against a method the product no longer exercises, and future editors maintaining the subtitle formatting are maintaining a path that can never run.

[ADVISORY] CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template creates a base-class-to-sibling coupling: the commit-context ABC now hard-depends on PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, placing PR-comment presentation logic in the commit-context layer. Any CommitContextIntegration implementation that is not a PRCommentWorkflow (the ABC's actual contract) cannot use this method without importing the PR workflow class, and the next refactor of PRCommentWorkflow's helpers breaks commit_context from below — the ownership boundary between the two abstractions is now crossed in one direction only, invisibly.

[BUG] The migration body was silently gutted to a no-op (`return`) with a comment pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, which is not added anywhere in this diff, so the org-saved-searches-to-views conversion intent was dropped without a replacement landing in the same change. Any environment that has not yet executed migration 0917 (fresh installs and environments upgrading across this commit) never converts organization saved searches into GroupSearchViews, so the views feature silently shows empty/missing data for existing org saved searches — a data-conversion objective that was accepted in the original migration design is now unfulfilled.

[BUG] The revised migration 0920 was also gutted to a no-op referencing the same absent `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, meaning both originally-intended conversion paths were removed in review iterations while the successor migration is not part of this artifact. Environments upgrading past this commit run two migrations that do nothing; if 0921 does not already exist on the target branch, the org saved search conversion is permanently lost for those environments because both intended carriers of the intent were disabled.

[BUG] The product-wide default `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` was silently flipped from `"low"` to `"off"` inside a PR whose stated objective is the Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System — a behavioral objective change with no feature flag, no migration, and no visible human acceptance. Every new project created after deploy gets autofix automation fully disabled by default instead of `low`; existing operators who relied on the documented default silently lose automatic autofix runs for new issues, and the change is undiscoverable from the PR title or changelog intent.

[BUG] The project-option default `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` was flipped from `"low"` to `"off"` at a second, independent declaration site, completing the same unaccepted default change begun in constants.py. New projects materialize the project option with `off`, so no autofix automation runs for them; because this default is duplicated across two files, any future partial reversion of one site leaves the two declarations inconsistent, and this behavior change rides in under a replay-bulk-delete PR where it cannot be traced to an accepted decision.

[ADVISORY] The PR titled 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System' contains only one in-scope change (a 5-line null-segment guard here) while carrying at least a dozen unrelated objectives — browser collector rewrite, PR comment template redesign, detector owner field, delayed-workflow refactor, taskworker deadlines, autofix default flips, migration gutting, prompt rewrites, and bulk frontend refactors — indicating review iterations accreted objectives that were never re-accepted against the stated intent. Reviewers and bisecters cannot attribute regressions to the stated objective: a future revert of 'the bulk delete fix' either drags ten unrelated behavior changes with it or requires archaeology to separate them; the pattern also means each unrelated change (e.g., the autofix default flip) bypassed focused review of its own intent.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's accepted-input contract silently narrowed from permissive (every report counted, 200 returned) to strict all-or-nothing validation: any single invalid report in a browser's batch now returns 422 and drops every valid report in the same POST, whereas the previous code processed each report independently. Real browsers POST multiple reports per batch and do not retry rejected collector POSTs, so one malformed report (e.g., a report type outside BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES or attempts < 1 from a spec-divergent browser) now causes the telemetry loss of all co-batched valid reports — a metric-counting behavior change embedded in an unrelated PR without an explicit contract decision.

[ADVISORY] The merged-PR comment format was silently redesigned: the bullet changed from `-` to `*`, the `{subtitle}` (culprit) field was removed from the template entirely, and a 50-char title truncation plus environment suffix were added — user-visible output changes under the replays PR title. Users who parse or visually rely on the culprit line in merged-PR bot comments lose that signal with no flag or option to restore the old format; because the old `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` constants were deleted from both github/integration.py and gitlab/integration.py in the same diff, the format change is irreversible per-deployment without a code revert.

[ADVISORY] The `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` capability and its backing option registration (`grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` in options/defaults.py) were silently deleted, removing an experiment pathway whose kill-switch no longer exists. Any environment that still has the traceparent parameterization option enabled at a nonzero rate silently stops running that experiment — the `should_run` gate now guards nothing for regex experiments, and operators who try to disable/reenable the behavior via the removed option get a no-op with no error, masking the intent that the experiment was supposed to be measurable and reversible.

[ADVISORY] The new validation-failure path logs the raw attacker-controlled report body ('raw_report': report) plus serializer errors at warning level from an unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint. Any unauthenticated internet caller can write arbitrarily chosen, unlimited-volume content into warning-level operational logs (log flooding/storage cost, and injection of attacker-authored entries into log streams that on-call and alerting tooling consume); the payload is reflected verbatim into log pipeline before any allowlist filtering.

[ADVISORY] The new PR-comment template interpolates the user-controlled issue title (and, via get_environment_info, the environment name) into markdown posted to GitHub/GitLab without any escaping. An attacker who controls event data (any SDK user) can craft an issue title containing markdown metacharacters (e.g. 'x](https://evil.example) [y'), which break out of the '[**{title}**]({url})' construct and inject arbitrary links/formatting into Sentry-bot-authored PR comments on third-party repositories — a phishing/link-injection vector in developer-facing surfaces; the 50-char truncation does not strip markdown syntax.

[BUG] The mutual-exclusion validation in validate_timestamp/validate_age uses truthiness checks (`if self.initial_data.get("age")` / `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`), so age=0 paired with a timestamp (or timestamp=0 paired with an age) passes validation even though the code's stated rule is that the two fields are mutually exclusive. A browser report containing both age=0 and a non-zero timestamp is accepted and recorded, defeating the cross-spec disambiguation the validators exist to enforce; a test submitting age=0 + timestamp would expose this, and any consumer relying on the exclusion invariant gets ambiguous payload semantics.

[BUG] The endpoint validates every report before processing any, so a single invalid report in a multi-report POST returns 422 and discards all valid reports in the same batch (metrics.incr never runs for them). Browsers deliver reports in batches; one malformed or unrecognized report type (e.g., a new spec report type added by a browser before BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES is updated) silently drops the metrics for every valid report in that request, since per the Reporting API non-2xx responses cause reports to be discarded rather than retried individually.

[BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against nodestore get_multi's values (`zip(error_ids, events.values())`), but get_multi omits keys whose nodes are missing, so the first absent event shifts every subsequent (event_id, data) pair and misattributes title/message/timestamp to the wrong error id. When any event has expired from nodestore (normal for older replays), the Seer summarize prompt is built with the wrong error title/message attached to each error id and one error is silently dropped, producing a replay summary that cites errors the user did not experience at those points; a test with a missing node id would expose the misalignment.

[ADVISORY] The new error-context feature only works if the caller happens to pass `field=error_ids` in the query string (error_ids is read out of process_raw_response rows built from `request.query_params.getlist("field")`), and only row 0's error_ids are used (`response[0].get(...)`), so the feature silently no-ops otherwise. Any API consumer (including the frontend integration being built against this endpoint) that calls GET without the exact field parameter gets a 200 response with zero error context and no signal that anything was skipped; a test that doesn't replicate the caller's exact field parameter would green-light a build where the feature never fires.

[ADVISORY] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) executes before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before any request validation, so requests that are subsequently rejected (feature disabled, invalid checkpoint) are still recorded as assemble events. Analytics dashboards counting assemble events are inflated by denied and malformed requests, and the counts cannot be distinguished from successful assembles because no outcome is attached to the event; teams consuming this event for adoption metrics get misleading numbers from day one.

[BUG] MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE ends with a literal `\n` while both call sites assemble the list with `"\n".join(...)`, producing a blank line between every issue entry plus a trailing blank line, where the deleted per-integration templates produced a compact list. GitHub and GitLab merged-PR comments render with an empty line between each issue bullet and a trailing empty line before the footer, a visible formatting regression versus the previous single-newline list; existing tests that assert the exact comment body will either fail (catching it) or were updated to encode the double-spacing as expected behavior.

[ADVISORY] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template, a static method on CommitContextIntegration, invokes `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` even though `_truncate_title` is defined on CommitContextIntegration itself in this same diff, coupling the integration base class to the workflow class for a helper it already owns. Title-truncation ownership now spans two unrelated class hierarchies: if PRCommentWorkflow does not actually define _truncate_title, every merged-PR comment render raises AttributeError; even if it does, the next change to truncation rules must be applied in two places, and a test mocking at either class boundary can pass while the other path diverges.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation tuning default is duplicated in two independently maintained registrations — DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in constants.py and `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` in projectoptions/defaults.py — and this diff had to flip both from "low" to "off" in lockstep. The next person changing this default (or adding a third tuning level) must know to update both sites; updating only one yields orgs and projects silently disagreeing on the default, and no test pins the two constants to each other so the drift ships unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] Rewriting the previously-shipped data migration 0917 into a no-op leaves no remediation path for any database that already recorded it as applied and ran the original unfiltered conversion, which created GroupSearchView rows with user_id=saved_search.owner_id (NULL for ownerless organization saved searches, since the original body lacked the owner_id__isnull=False filter that 0920 added). Self-hosted installs (or any environment) that applied a release containing 0917 before the error was discovered keep whatever rows the buggy conversion produced; the no-op body and the 0921 re-run (update_or_create keyed on organization/user_id/name) never match or delete the null-owner rows, so stale orphan views persist indefinitely and no step in this diff cleans them up.

[BUG] fetch_error_details catches every exception from nodestore.backend.get_multi and returns [], so a nodestore outage or deserialization failure silently degrades the summarize response to an error-free summary while the endpoint returns HTTP 200. The caller (frontend summarize flow) cannot distinguish 'this replay had no errors' from 'error fetching failed', so Seer generates and the user receives a breadcrumb summary that silently omits all error context; the only trace is a captured Sentry event operators may not act on. This is exactly the invisible-failure pattern: the user-facing operation reports success while dropping work.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's core new behavior (error context) depends on the client passing field=error_ids in the query string: error_ids is read from process_raw_response(request.query_params.getlist("field")) output with a silent .get(..., []) fallback. Any caller that hits the endpoint without field=error_ids (new SDK consumers, curl testing, a frontend regression that drops the param) gets a 200 response with the error-context feature silently no-op'd — no validation error, no log — and Seer summarizes breadcrumbs only. Staff-worthy because the endpoint should request error_ids itself rather than depending on a caller-supplied field list for internal behavior.

[ADVISORY] error_events is fetched once and captured via functools.partial into on_results, but gen_request_data resets error_idx to 0 per call, so every paginated page's Seer request includes the replay's full error list merged against only that page's segments. Errors from later time ranges are injected into earlier pages' prompts (and every error appears in every page's summary request), so multi-page replays produce duplicated and chronologically wrong summaries, and each page's Seer payload grows with the total error count rather than the page's share.

[ADVISORY] fetch_error_details issues nodestore.backend.get_multi with one node_id per snuba-returned error_id and no cap on the list size. An error-spam replay with hundreds/thousands of distinct error_ids makes a correspondingly large nodestore fan-out synchronously inside this GET request path, inflating latency and risking endpoint timeouts; there is no max() on the number of error IDs fetched per request.

[ADVISORY] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) fires at the top of post() before the feature gate and all validation, so requests that are subsequently rejected are recorded as assemble events. The preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics series counts 403 feature-gate denials and later validation failures as successful assemble invocations, and attributes them to the requesting user — anyone consuming this event for adoption/funnel metrics gets inflated, unfaithful data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint's accepted-input contract silently narrowed from permissive (every report counted, 200 returned) to strict all-or-nothing validation: any single invalid report in a browser's batch now returns 422 and drops every valid report in the same POST, whereas the previous code processed each report independently. Real browsers POST multiple reports per batch and do not retry rejected collector POSTs, so one malformed report (e.g., a report type outside BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES or attempts < 1 from a spec-divergent browser) now causes the telemetry loss of all co-batched valid reports — a metric-counting behavior change embedded in an unrelated PR without an explicit contract decision.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post` now validates each report with `BrowserReportSerializer` and immediately `return Response(..., 422)` on the first invalid item (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(...)`), so a mixed-validity batch results in zero metrics recorded for any later valid reports. Previously, the endpoint iterated all items and unconditionally `metrics.incr(...)` for each constructed `BrowserReport`, with no runtime validation of `type` (Literal isn’t enforced), so e.g. an unknown `type` would still be counted as long as required keys existed. While the old code was also fragile (missing/extra fields would raise during `BrowserReport(**report)`), the specific “all-or-nothing” behavior for per-item validation failures is a real behavior/contract change grounded in the diff and worth an explicit decision.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new validation-failure path logs the raw attacker-controlled report body ('raw_report': report) plus serializer errors at warning level from an unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint. Any unauthenticated internet caller can write arbitrarily chosen, unlimited-volume content into warning-level operational logs (log flooding/storage cost, and injection of attacker-authored entries into log streams that on-call and alerting tooling consume); the payload is reflected verbatim into log pipeline before any allowlist filtering.

This endpoint is explicitly unauthenticated (`permission_classes = ()`) and CSRF-exempt (`@csrf_exempt`), so any caller can submit arbitrary JSON and cause attacker-controlled content (`report`) to be written verbatim into warning-level logs (and `serializer.errors` can also include attacker-supplied values like the invalid `type`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new PR-comment template interpolates the user-controlled issue title (and, via get_environment_info, the environment name) into markdown posted to GitHub/GitLab without any escaping. An attacker who controls event data (any SDK user) can craft an issue title containing markdown metacharacters (e.g. 'x](https://evil.example) [y'), which break out of the '[**{title}**]({url})' construct and inject arbitrary links/formatting into Sentry-bot-authored PR comments on third-party repositories — a phishing/link-injection vector in developer-facing surfaces; the 50-char truncation does not strip markdown syntax.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new markdown template for PR comments in `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"`, and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` formats it with `title=...` (derived from `issue.title`) and `environment=self.get_environment_info(issue)` (derived from `environment.name`) without any escaping/sanitization. Since issue titles and environment names can be influenced by event data, markdown metacharacters (e.g., `](`, backticks) could break out of the intended link/text formatting and inject arbitrary links/formatting into bot-authored GitHub/GitLab comments. The added 50-char truncation (`_truncate_title`) does not remove/escape markdown syntax, so it does not mitigate injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The mutual-exclusion validation in validate_timestamp/validate_age uses truthiness checks (`if self.initial_data.get("age")` / `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`), so age=0 paired with a timestamp (or timestamp=0 paired with an age) passes validation even though the code's stated rule is that the two fields are mutually exclusive. A browser report containing both age=0 and a non-zero timestamp is accepted and recorded, defeating the cross-spec disambiguation the validators exist to enforce; a test submitting age=0 + timestamp would expose this, and any consumer relying on the exclusion invariant gets ambiguous payload semantics.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags the same core bug: mutual-exclusion validation uses `self.initial_data.get(...)`/truthiness checks, so a value of 0 is treated as missing and can incorrectly pass validation. This aligns with the golden comment’s point that `get('timestamp')` (and similarly `get('age')`) mishandles 0 and should use explicit key-presence checks like `'timestamp' in self.initial_data`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The endpoint validates every report before processing any, so a single invalid report in a multi-report POST returns 422 and discards all valid reports in the same batch (metrics.incr never runs for them). Browsers deliver reports in batches; one malformed or unrecognized report type (e.g., a new spec report type added by a browser before BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES is updated) silently drops the metrics for every valid report in that request, since per the Reporting API non-2xx responses cause reports to be discarded rather than retried individually.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`, the POST handler validates the entire `raw_data` batch first and immediately returns `Response(..., status=422)` on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(...)`). Metrics are only emitted in a second loop after validation completes. Therefore, a single invalid/unknown report (e.g., `type` not in `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES`) causes the endpoint to return 422 and **no** `metrics.incr("browser_reporting.raw_report_received", ...)` calls happen for any other valid reports in the same request. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details zips error_ids against nodestore get_multi's values (`zip(error_ids, events.values())`), but get_multi omits keys whose nodes are missing, so the first absent event shifts every subsequent (event_id, data) pair and misattributes title/message/timestamp to the wrong error id. adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can misalign IDs to event data. It specifically explains that `get_multi` may omit missing keys, shifting the remaining values and misattributing data—one of the key failure modes described in the golden comment (and implicitly relies on value order matching input IDs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The autofix automation tuning default is duplicated in two independently maintained registrations — DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in constants.py and `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` in projectoptions/defaults.py — and this diff had to flip both from "low" to "off" in lockstep. The next person changing this default (or adding a third tuning level) must know to update both sites; updating only one yields orgs and projects silently disagreeing on the default, and no test pins the two constants to each other so the drift ships unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the same default being maintained in two places: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` in `src/sentry/constants.py` was changed from "low" to "off", and the project option registration `register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default=...)` in `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` was also changed from "low" to "off". This demonstrates the duplication and the need to update both in lockstep. The updated tests (`tests/sentry/api/endpoints/test_project_details.py`, `tests/sentry/api/serializers/test_project.py`) assert the project option default value, but nothing in the diff verifies that the constants default and the registered option default are linked or equal, so drift could go unnoticed. This is a maintainability/architecture concern rather than a current functional defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Rewriting the previously-shipped data migration 0917 into a no-op leaves no remediation path for any database that already recorded it as applied and ran the original unfiltered conversion, which created GroupSearchView rows with user_id=saved_search.owner_id (NULL for ownerless organization saved searches, since the original body lacked the owner_id__isnull=False filter that 0920 added). Self-hosted installs (or any environment) that applied a release containing 0917 before the error was discovered keep whatever rows the buggy conversion produced; the no-op body and the 0921 re-run (update_or_create keyed on organization/user_id/name) never match or delete the null-owner rows, so stale orphan views persist indefinitely and no step in this diff cleans them up.

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites both `0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py` and `0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py` into unconditional no-ops (`return`) and deletes the 0917 migration test. Regardless of the comment claiming they “were never run,” the diff itself provides no remediation/cleanup migration for any installation that may already have applied 0917/0920 when they still contained conversion logic. If those migrations ever ran in the wild, making them no-ops removes the ability for Django’s migration framework to re-run/repair them (since they’re recorded as applied), and this diff does not add any corrective step to reconcile or delete potentially-bad `GroupSearchView` rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details catches every exception from nodestore.backend.get_multi and returns [], so a nodestore outage or deserialization failure silently degrades the summarize response to an error-free summary while the endpoint returns HTTP 200. The caller (frontend summarize flow) cannot distinguish 'this replay had no errors' from 'error fetching failed', so Seer generates and the user receives a breadcrumb summary that silently omits all error context; the only trace is a captured Sentry event operators may not act on. This is exactly the invisible-failure pattern: the user-facing operation reports success while dropping work.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the new `fetch_error_details()` wraps `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` in a broad `try/except` and on any exception does `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)` then returns `[]`. The endpoint then proceeds to call `analyze_recording_segments`/`make_seer_request` and returns `HTTP_200_OK` regardless, meaning a nodestore outage/deserialization error will be indistinguishable from “no errors” and will silently omit error context from the AI summary while still reporting success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint's core new behavior (error context) depends on the client passing field=error_ids in the query string: error_ids is read from process_raw_response(request.query_params.getlist("field")) output with a silent .get(..., []) fallback. Any caller that hits the endpoint without field=error_ids (new SDK consumers, curl testing, a frontend regression that drops the param) gets a 200 response with the error-context feature silently no-op'd — no validation error, no log — and Seer summarizes breadcrumbs only. Staff-worthy because the endpoint should request error_ids itself rather than depending on a caller-supplied field list for internal behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then `error_ids = response[0].get("error_ids", [])`, so it’s true that the returned shape could be influenced by `field`. However, the added server-side test `test_get_with_error` calls `self.client.get(self.url)` with no `field=error_ids` query param and still asserts that the Seer request logs include the error (meaning `error_ids` was present and used). That contradicts the finding’s core claim that callers without `field=error_ids` will silently get no error context. From the diff alone, the stronger interpretation is that `error_ids` is available without requiring a caller-supplied field list (or the test would fail).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] error_events is fetched once and captured via functools.partial into on_results, but gen_request_data resets error_idx to 0 per call, so every paginated page's Seer request includes the replay's full error list merged against only that page's segments. Errors from later time ranges are injected into earlier pages' prompts (and every error appears in every page's summary request), so multi-page replays produce duplicated and chronologically wrong summaries, and each page's Seer payload grows with the total error count rather than the page's share.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, `error_events` is fetched once per request and then passed into the paginator via `on_results=functools.partial(analyze_recording_segments, error_events)`. `analyze_recording_segments` calls `get_request_data(iter_segment_data(segments), error_events)`, which sorts the full `error_events` list and then `gen_request_data` initializes `error_idx = 0` and, critically, always yields any *remaining* errors after processing the page's segment events (`while error_idx < len(error_events): yield ...`). For earlier pages (earlier timestamps), later errors will be appended at the end, meaning each paginated page's Seer prompt includes errors outside that page’s time range and duplicates the full error list across pages, producing chronologically incorrect/duplicated summaries and payload growth with total errors rather than per-page errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_error_details issues nodestore.backend.get_multi with one node_id per snuba-returned error_id and no cap on the list size. An error-spam replay with hundreds/thousands of distinct error_ids makes a correspondingly large nodestore fan-out synchronously inside this GET request path, inflating latency and risking endpoint timeouts; there is no max() on the number of error IDs fetched per request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `fetch_error_details(project_id, error_ids)` in `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, which pulls `error_ids` from `query_replay_instance(...)` results and then unconditionally builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(... ) for id in error_ids]` and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` synchronously. There is no cap/limit applied to `error_ids` in this code path (and error context is enabled by default unless `enable_error_context=false` is passed). This is a concrete, diff-grounded scalability/latency risk (potential large fan-out per request), but it’s not a directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) fires at the top of post() before the feature gate and all validation, so requests that are subsequently rejected are recorded as assemble events. The preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics series counts 403 feature-gate denials and later validation failures as successful assemble invocations, and attributes them to the requesting user — anyone consuming this event for adoption/funnel metrics gets inflated, unfaithful data.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` was added at the start of `post()` before the feature gate check `if not features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)`. As a result, requests that are rejected with 403 due to the feature flag (and any later failures) will still emit the "api.assemble" analytics event, inflating/tainting that event stream with unsuccessful attempts attributed to the requesting user.
